subject: Career
title: Career Seasons: The Long Game
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Career Seasons: The Long Game.

hook.text: He sprinted for a decade. By 35, he was burned out, divorced, and rich. Was this success?

buildup.text: A 40-year career has seasons: sprints, recoveries, pivots, and plateaus. Treating it as one continuous sprint leads to burnout.

discovery.text: Brian Fetherstonhaugh's research: careers have three stages — fuel (learn), pivot (grow), and master (sustain).

twist.text: Most burnout happens when people try to sprint during a season meant for recovery or exploration.

climax.text: Ask: 'What season am I in?' Align your effort to the season, not to an arbitrary pace set by others.

punchline.text: Careers are marathons with seasons. Run yours accordingly.

quiz.question: What are Fetherstonhaugh's three career stages?

details.summary: Career seasons is a framework that views professional life as having natural periods of intense growth, harvest, rest, and reinvention rather than constant linear advancement. Understanding these rhythms helps normalize periods of lower intensity and prevents burnout from unrealistic expectations.
details.whyItMatters: The pressure to always be growing causes burnout when people fight natural career rhythms. Embracing career seasons allows strategic rest and reinvention that compound into greater long-term achievement.
takeaways: Careers naturally cycle through growth, harvest, rest, and reinvention
Rest seasons build capacity for the next growth phase
Constant upward pressure ignores natural professional rhythms

faq.question: How long does a typical career season last?
faq.answer: Career seasons vary widely by individual and context, typically lasting two to seven years each. Growth seasons often coincide with new roles or industries. Rest seasons may follow major achievements or life events. The key is recognizing your current season rather than predicting exact durations.

faq.question: How can someone tell which career season they are currently in?
faq.answer: Growth seasons feel energizing with steep learning curves. Harvest seasons involve leveraging established expertise. Rest seasons feature lower ambition and a need to recharge. Reinvention seasons bring restlessness and attraction to new directions..
